newsitem.title: GREECE: YOUNG GREEK-AMERICAN COMPLETES SOLO ATLANTIC SAIL.
newsitem.headline: YOUNG GREEK-AMERICAN COMPLETES SOLO ATLANTIC SAIL.

text.p: A young student said on Tuesday he had fullfilled his life-long dream by sailing alone across the Atlantic from the United States to his native Greece.
Sociology student Christos Papaliolios, 23, arrived in the port of Patras on the Peloponnese coast on Monday after sailing 6,000 nautical miles (10,800 kms) in three months.
"My driving force was my father," said Papaliolios, whose father is a ship's captain.
"Throughout my life he has told me that exploration in life is the most important thing, and the unexplored is not worth living, as Socrates said," he told Reuters television in Patras.
He arrived on the 25-foot (eight metre) sailboat "Teresa" which he bought for $3,500.
His parents and locals clapped and cheered as he arrived and held a banner aloft proclaiming: "Christos, for those who dare, watch out."
He completed the journey in a 35-year-old boat which he had bought after working as a waiter in a Manhattan restaurant.
"You made it," cried his mother Teresa, who he named the boat after.
Papaliolios, with only 16 months experience as a captain, slept for only four hours a day, and stayed awake for 48 hours during a storm near the Azores Islands.
"I was terrified," he said. "The wind was howling and the sea was raging. There was no one in sight. But in my most desperate moment, I found an amazing calm come over me."
The Greek merchant marine ministry checked his progress with trans-Atlantic ships to make sure he was okay.
"You wouldn't believe how worried we were," his mother told Reuters, "but we knew he could do it."
Papaliolios, who said he has acquired a deep respect for the ocean, is considering going around the world with his boat but said he will rest before another such undertaking.
